solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Abandoned, of course I will be wild (9)

indicatorNotes.Abandoned: abandoned means unrestrained, so the letters are let loose to fall into any order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Someone promises that once let off the leash they will run riot.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma tempts you to read 'Abandoned' as the definition; it is the anagram instruction, and the definition waits at the far end.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a fierce, savage animal is a wild one.

entries.clue: Shy away from Florida island (6)

blocks.note: FL is the postal abbreviation for Florida
an inch is a small Scottish island, as in Inchcolm

annotation.surface: A shy traveller keeps clear of an island off Florida.
annotation.walkthrough: The island here is Scottish, from Gaelic innis, and it turns up often in crosswords; nothing to do with the Florida Keys the surface suggests.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for a phrasal verb: to recoil from something in fear is to shy away from it.

entries.clue: Taking the Tube, run provided narrow path for divided area (4,6)

indicatorNotes.Taking: the rest of the wordplay takes the Tube in, holding it inside

blocks.note: r = run, the cricket scoring abbreviation
provided (that) = if
the tube = television, slang for the set
an alley is a narrow path between buildings

annotation.surface: A Londoner catches the Underground, then runs down a narrow path.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital T makes 'the Tube' look like the London Underground; it is slang for the television set.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a rift valley forms where the earth's crust splits apart, leaving land divided either side.

entries.clue: Treat as one or two-dimensional in 3D figure (8)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' puts the two-dimensional word inside the 3D figure

blocks.note: a cone is a solid, three-dimensional shape
a two-dimensional thing is flat

annotation.surface: A geometry lesson about flat and solid shapes.
annotation.walkthrough: The geometry picture hides the definition at the start, which is about merging ideas rather than shapes.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to merge two separate ideas into one is to treat them as one.

entries.clue: Australia cut off Japanese conductor (5)

indicatorNotes.cut: a word that is cut is trimmed short, losing its last letter

blocks.note: Oz is a nickname for Australia
off = AWAY, cut short by one letter

annotation.surface: Australia has banned a visiting Japanese maestro.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cut off' reads as one verb in the surface; it splits into 'cut' (trim) and 'off' (away). Seiji Ozawa led the Boston Symphony Orchestra for nearly thirty years.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Seiji Ozawa was a celebrated Japanese orchestral conductor.

entries.clue: Estate possibly blocking two thirds of Midland city upset intimidating figure in his field? (9)

indicatorNotes.possibly: an estate is one possible kind of car, so 'possibly' marks a definition by example
indicatorNotes.blocking: the car blocks the road by sitting in the middle of the other letters
indicatorNotes.two thirds of: two thirds of a nine-letter city is its first six letters
indicatorNotes.upset: in a down clue, upset turns the letters upside down, so they read backwards

blocks.note: Worcester, a city in the English Midlands, minus its last third (TER)
an estate is a British car body style (a station wagon)

annotation.surface: A car parked across the road leaves a Midlands city upset.
annotation.walkthrough: An estate car is what Americans call a station wagon. The question mark flags that 'his field' is a literal field of crops, not an area of expertise.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a scarecrow stands in a field to frighten birds off.

entries.clue: Order having the benefit of ignoring leaders of youth groups (6)

indicatorNotes.ignoring: to ignore letters is to leave them out
indicatorNotes.leaders of: the leaders of words are their first letters

blocks.note: to enjoy good health is to have the benefit of it
first letters of youth and groups, both left out

annotation.surface: A directive on who may use a benefit, excluding youth-group heads.
annotation.walkthrough: Enjoy has the sense 'possess', as in enjoying a right, which is how it can mean having the benefit of something.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to enjoin someone to act is to order or instruct them to.

entries.clue: Cork sweetener for plonk? (4)

blocks.note: a stopper for a bottle or cask
British slang for a bribe
to put something down carelessly

annotation.surface: A wine question: is a cork the thing that improves cheap plonk?
annotation.walkthrough: Really a triple definition: 'plonk' is cheap wine in the surface but also the verb meaning to dump something down carelessly.
annotation.definitionFit: Three senses: a stopper, a slang bribe, and a verb for tossing something down.

entries.clue: Lanthanum used in reconstruction of Nordic warship (8)

indicatorNotes.used in: the element is used in the rebuild, going inside it
indicatorNotes.reconstruction of: a reconstruction rebuilds the word's letters in a new order

blocks.note: NORDIC rearranged
La is the chemical symbol for lanthanum

annotation.surface: A museum team rebuilds a Viking longship using a rare-earth metal.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface wants a Viking longship; the warship is a 19th-century armoured steamship.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: ironclads were steam warships protected by iron plating.

entries.clue: Trick question curtailed win (7)

indicatorNotes.curtailed: curtailed literally means with the tail cut off, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: a con is a trick or swindle
QUERY without its last letter

annotation.surface: A quiz contestant wins with a trick question cut short.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trick question' reads as one phrase in the surface; it splits into two separate pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to overcome an enemy is to win against them.

entries.clue: Supporter cheers on popular princess (7)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, one piece placed on another comes after it

blocks.note: in = fashionable, popular
a fan supports a team or star
ta is British slang for thanks, as is cheers

annotation.surface: A fan cheers on a well-loved princess.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' is applause in the surface; here it means thanks, which the British also say as 'ta'.
annotation.definitionFit: A foreign title: an infanta is a daughter of the Spanish or Portuguese monarch.

entries.clue: Maybe heart stops affecting supply to one’s pipes (5)

annotation.definition2: stops affecting supply to one’s pipes

blocks.note: the heart is one example of a vital body part

blocks.clueFragment: stops affecting supply to one’s pipes
blocks.note: the instrument's stops control which pipes get air

annotation.surface: A cardiac arrest cuts the blood supply to the body's pipes.
annotation.walkthrough: The medical surface reads 'stops' as a verb and 'pipes' as blood vessels; they are the knobs and pipes of a church instrument.
annotation.definitionFit: A body part given by example, and the keyboard instrument described by its stops and pipes.

entries.clue: Fall with Valerie for Singleton’s first procession (9)

indicatorNotes.for: one thing given for another is exchanged for it, so VAL is swapped in for S
indicatorNotes.first: a word's first is its opening letter

blocks.note: a cascade is a waterfall
Valerie cut down to her first three letters, the usual short form
first letter of Singleton, swapped out

annotation.surface: Valerie Singleton, the children's TV presenter, fronting a waterfall piece.
annotation.walkthrough: Valerie Singleton was a long-serving Blue Peter presenter on British children's TV, so the two names look like one person; they are separate pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a cavalcade is a formal procession, originally one of riders on horseback.

entries.clue: Set fuel to burn, suppressing naked anger (7)

indicatorNotes.suppressing: to suppress is to hold down inside, so the fuel keeps the anger within it
indicatorNotes.naked: a naked word is stripped of its outer letters

blocks.note: coal is fuel for burning
ANGER without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: Someone lays a fire to work off their fury.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Set' at the start looks like a verb meaning arrange or lay; it means solidify.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a liquid that congeals thickens and sets.

entries.clue: Perhaps a blow, being all in when Louisiana stands for America (10)

indicatorNotes.stands for: one thing that stands for another takes its place, so LA replaces US

blocks.note: all in = worn out, exhausted
LA is the postal abbreviation for Louisiana
US = America, the letters swapped out

annotation.surface: An exhausted boxer takes a punch while a US state stands in for the nation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blow' suggests a punch after 'all in'; it is a puff of breath. 'Perhaps' marks a blow as one kind of breathing out.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: blowing out candles is one kind of breathing out.

entries.clue: Instrument for period recording? (5)

blocks.note: the surface wants a musical instrument, as in a period instrument
read literally: a device whose job is to record how long a period of time lasts

annotation.surface: Early music: which instrument is authentic for a period-performance recording?
annotation.walkthrough: 'Period instrument' and 'recording' conjure early music on authentic instruments; read literally, the instrument records a stretch of time.
annotation.definitionFit: Read literally: a kitchen or egg timer is an instrument that measures a set period.

entries.clue: Dreadful tedium gripping last month’s host (9)

indicatorNotes.Dreadful: dreadful means in a bad state, so the letters come out mangled
indicatorNotes.gripping: the rearranged letters grip the abbreviation, holding it inside

blocks.note: TEDIUM rearranged
ult. (ultimo) = of last month, in old business letters

annotation.surface: A dull evening at which the host held everyone's attention.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Host' looks like the person throwing the party; it means a great crowd, as in a heavenly host.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a host, as in 'a host of golden daffodils', is a great number.

entries.clue: Feel embarrassed somewhat about scrap (5)

indicatorNotes.somewhat: somewhat means only to some extent, so only some of the letters are used
indicatorNotes.about: about means turned around, so the run reads backwards

blocks.note: f(EEL EM)barrassed

annotation.surface: Someone is a little embarrassed about a scrap of something.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' reads as a small piece; it is a fight.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a confused brawl is a scrap, British slang for a fight.

entries.clue: Airborne pest miles over southern capital (8)

blocks.note: m = miles
o = over, from cricket scorecards
s = southern
Quito is the capital of Ecuador

annotation.surface: A pest carried by air for miles above a southern capital.
annotation.walkthrough: Quito sits almost on the equator, so a biting insect over it fits the surface neatly.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a flying, biting insect is an airborne pest.

entries.clue: Sucker pronounced not entirely safe, idiomatically (5)

indicatorNotes.pronounced: what is pronounced is spoken, so the letters count for their sound
indicatorNotes.not entirely: not all of the words are used, only a run of letters inside them

blocks.note: s(AFE ID)iomatically, said as one word

annotation.surface: A gullible person is told something is not quite safe, as the saying goes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sucker' looks like a dupe; it is a sap-sucking insect. The hidden letters are spelt wrongly but sound right.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: this greenfly feeds by sucking sap from plants.

entries.clue: Ruse, ie craft I devised (8)

indicatorNotes.devised: something devised is invented or worked out, so the letters are worked into something new

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: A schemer boasts of a ruse, a crafty plan they came up with.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is almost literal: craft that I devised is itself trickery.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a clever trick or stratagem is a ruse.

entries.clue: Reduce glare (5)

blocks.note: to bring prices down
to scowl, a word also spelt lour

annotation.surface: An instruction to cut down dazzling light.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Glare' reads as bright light but is the angry look; in that sense the word rhymes with 'power', not 'slower'.
annotation.definitionFit: Two verbs spelt alike: one means bring down, the other (rhyming with 'flower') means scowl.

entries.clue: Designer of roster for pig-farmer? (7)

blocks.note: someone who designs hair or clothes
a list for a pigsty

annotation.surface: Who draws up the duty rota on a pig farm?
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the made-up second reading, split as two words: a rota for the pigs' pen.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the designer of hair or fashion, plus a whimsical split into sty + list.

entries.clue: Helping served up during pub’s spicy meal (6)

indicatorNotes.served up: in a down clue, up means the word reads bottom to top
indicatorNotes.during: one thing during another sits inside it

blocks.note: aid = help
an inn is a pub

annotation.surface: A helping of food is dished up at the pub's curry night.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Helping' is a portion of food in the surface; it means help. In Britain 'going for an Indian' means going out for a curry.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: in Britain an Indian is a curry meal, usually from a restaurant or takeaway.

entries.clue: Unionist who might make sparks fly with senior adviser (6)

annotation.definition: Unionist who might make sparks fly

blocks.note: w = with, as in w/
a church elder is a senior adviser

annotation.surface: A trade unionist causes a row with a senior counsellor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unionist' suggests a trade union or Ulster politics; this worker unites pieces of metal, and 'make sparks fly' is literal.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: a worker who unites metal parts, with sparks flying from the torch.

entries.clue: Drip caught by painter working secretly (2,7)

indicatorNotes.caught by: what is caught by something is held inside it
indicatorNotes.working: letters that are working are active, moved about into a new order

blocks.note: PAINTER rearranged
an IV (intravenous) drip in hospital

annotation.surface: An artist is caught quietly dripping paint while at work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drip' fits a painter's work, but it is the hospital kind, fed into a vein.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: doing something away from others' eyes is doing it secretly.

entries.clue: These are very desirable vocal sounds (5)

blocks.note: as in the choice jobs everyone wants
rich, deep tones of voice, as in a plummy accent

annotation.surface: A comment that some voices are lovely to listen to.
annotation.walkthrough: A 'plummy' voice is a posh British one, as if spoken with a fruit in the mouth.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses of the fruit: the best pickings, and the rich tone of a posh voice.

entries.clue: Single or plural pronoun in conjunction for Germans (5)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' puts the pronoun inside the German word

blocks.note: und is German for 'and'
we is a plural pronoun

annotation.surface: A German grammar lesson on singular and plural pronouns.
annotation.walkthrough: The grammar surface makes 'Single' look like 'singular'; it means not married.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who has never married is single.

entries.clue: Nothing detracted from outstanding side of building (4)

indicatorNotes.detracted from: to detract is to take away, so the nothing is removed

blocks.note: a sum outstanding is still owing
o = zero, nothing, taken away

annotation.surface: Nothing spoils the fine side of a building.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' means excellent in the surface; here it means unpaid.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a section projecting from the main block is a side of the building.

entries.clue: Made one female in two for wife of 25 (7)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' puts the female inside the two
indicatorNotes.for: one thing put for another is exchanged for it, so the new letters replace the wife

blocks.note: the answer to 25 across
Roman numeral two
f = female, inside the II
w = wife, swapped out

annotation.surface: A wedding pairs one female with another, uniting the two.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue borrows 25 across's answer, and swapping one letter turns the word for unmarried into one about joining. A neat pairing.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: things brought together into a single whole have been made one.

entries.clue: Fail ’eavily, being a mug (7)

indicatorNotes.’eavily: the apostrophe shows a dropped H, so the synonym drops its H too

blocks.note: a show that tanks fails
heavily = HARD, said without its H

annotation.surface: A Cockney admits failing badly, being a fool.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mug' is British slang for a dupe, which suits the surface; it is a drinking vessel. Heavily = hard, as in rain falling hard.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a large handled beer vessel is a kind of mug.

entries.clue: Harder to track each person in a rightish district? (9)

indicatorNotes.to track: to track something is to follow it, so the second piece comes after

blocks.note: ea. = each
sterner = harder, stricter

annotation.surface: Is a right-wing area harder on its people?
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rightish' suggests politics; on a map east is on the right, which the question mark admits.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: someone living in the east lives on the right-hand side of a map.
